item.title: 12 killed, 16 injured as bus carrying oil and gas workers overturns in Iran
item.description: A serious bus accident occurred in Iran's western Ilam Province, claiming the lives of 12 individuals. The bus was carrying employees of a natural gas liquids company when it overturned on Saturday night. Six ambulances and rescue vehicles were deployed to provide medical assistance to the 16 injured passengers. Authorities warned that the death toll might increase due to some victims' critical conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Iran has 1,500-2,500 missiles despite US claims of ‘decimated’ arsenal: Report
item.description: Iran's missile arsenal is estimated to consist of between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles, showcasing a significant military capacity. Both US and Israeli evaluations highlight Iran's resurgence in missile capabilities, despite previous airstrikes targeting production sites. Enhanced military strategies and precise targeting have allowed Iran to improve its striking effectiveness. The secretive nature of Iran's stockpiles and numerous producers complicate estimates, underscoring the necessity for vigilance among American and allied forces.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Co-op Owner Ordered To Allow Repairs: Court orders shower work; building seeks $170,000 in fees
item.description: A homeowner in Manhattan's Castle Village complex is involved in a legal battle regarding alleged water damage. The building claims the homeowner’s shower caused the damage, necessitating repairs at her expense. Multiple inspections failed to confirm the building's claims, leading to court decisions favoring both sides. Eventually, an appellate court ruled in favor of the building, requiring the homeowner to allow repairs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man rescues 1,132 ancient Mexican artefacts from Massachusetts dumpster; 40 students spend two years cataloguing them
item.description: During a house clearance in Massachusetts, over 1,100 fascinating pre-Hispanic archaeological items were rescued from a dumpster. Matthew Pioggia, noticing their historical significance, enlisted archaeologist Jeremy Pilver for help. Together with more than 40 high school students, they meticulously documented and cleaned these artifacts over nearly two years, unveiling their southeastern Mexican origins. In August 2026, the collection was respectfully returned to the Mexican Consulate in Boston.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak claims nearly half of infected as cases cross 11,000
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 11,000 cases and high fatalities. Basic health measures are inadequate, with most cases detected outside surveillance systems. Children are particularly affected, contributing to rising death rates due to lack of care. Attacks on health workers and facilities have further complicated containment efforts.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: ‘Utterly ridiculous take’: US official rejects report claiming Quad is on ‘life support’ under Trump
item.description: The United States has dismissed a media report suggesting the Quad alliance is struggling under the Trump administration. Senior State Department official Dylan Johnson called the assessment utterly ridiculous and highlighted regular diplomatic engagements among the four countries. A potential leaders' summit in Manila is set to be formalized during upcoming ASEAN meetings.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Chicago photographer's $220 thrift store paintings sell for $135,000 after rare discovery
item.description: In an unexpected twist of fate, a photographer from Chicago stumbled upon two remarkable original pieces by Warner Sallman in a thrift store back in 2016. After investing $220 for them, his diligence paid off two years later when he sold the artworks to author Jerry Jenkins for an impressive $135,000, reshaping the market landscape for Sallman’s creations and showcasing the hidden treasures often overlooked in thrift shops.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hungarian investigators found $19.5 million in cash buried in forests and hidden in buildings while probing allegations against a former minister
item.description: Hungary's anti-corruption efforts have yielded significant results, uncovering over $19.5 million in cash, stashed away in forests and hidden properties. Former minister Miklós Seszták faces bribery charges tied to the transport sector, while Prime Minister Peter Magyar's initiative seeks to address corruption issues involving the previous administration of Viktor Orbán. The Fidesz party has distanced itself from Seszták's allegations and calls for him to defend his reputation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Skeletons Cheer Cancer Patient: Ohio display encouraged Tammy during treatment; figures stay out year-round
item.description: In Oxford, Ohio, Bill Pyle's Halloween skeleton display became a beacon of hope for Tammy during her cancer journey. After receiving a touching letter, Pyle arranged the skeletons to honor her final radiation treatment, which shifted his perspective and deepened community bonds. This display is now a year-round fixture, updated weekly, with an annual homage to Tammy, illustrating how simple decorations can uplift during tough times.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘These tricks don’t work on me’: Eisenkot rejects Netanyahu’s 'unity govt' appeal
item.description: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated his call for a national unity government. Gadi Eisenkot, his political rival, dismissed Netanyahu's appeal, viewing it as a strategy to create division. Eisenkot is currently negotiating to form his government, with a deadline of 28 days. Discussions are strained over the Knesset speaker election, with both sides presenting opposing candidates. Netanyahu's coalition proposal excludes Arab parties, complicating the negotiations ahead.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Tens of thousands protest across Portugal over soaring housing costs
item.description: Protests occurred in over 30 cities across Portugal, reflecting increasing frustration over rising housing costs and insufficient incomes. Many protesters, including students and professionals, expressed concern about the affordability of housing. Demonstrators called for stronger tenant protections and limits on rent increases amidst growing inequality. The government promised to implement measures for affordable housing but acknowledged that changes will take time.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: UK PM Burnham's speechwriter caught using ChatGPT to draft speech
item.description: An anonymous speechwriter for Prime Minister Andy Burnham was seen using ChatGPT to draft a keynote address. The speech focused on criticizing former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher's legacy and addressing the cost-of-living crisis. Burnham emphasized the importance of these issues during his talk with Welsh Labour members. Opposition members have criticized both the aide's actions and Burnham’s government's plans to address economic challenges.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: US judge halts Trump's plan to close historic DC golf course for redevelopment
item.description: A US judge has issued a temporary block on President Trump's plan to close East Potomac Park. The ruling comes amid a legal challenge regarding the redevelopment of the historic public golf course. US District Judge Ana Reyes found that the government violated federal laws in seeking the closure. Trump plans to replace the existing courses with an 18-hole championship-level facility for major tournaments.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Swiss men take to streets, call for stronger fight against violence against women
item.description: Men gathered in the Swiss capital to protest against misogyny and violence directed at women. The demonstration called for men to take an active role in opposing misogynistic views, especially online. Organizers stressed the need for men to acknowledge their responsibility in challenging these attitudes. The event followed increased awareness of violence committed by men, highlighting the importance of addressing harmful masculinity.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Hamas confirms death of senior commander Samir Abu Younis in Israeli airstrike
item.description: In a recent Israeli airstrike, senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis was killed in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis, an incident that also left many injured. Known for his involvement in the planning of the deadly October 7 assault on Israel, his funeral is set for Sunday. The ongoing conflict continues to claim significant casualties on both sides since the ceasefire in October 2025.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Prince William, Kate to arrive in India in first joint overseas tour since 2022
item.description: Kate Middleton will join Prince William in Mumbai for the 2026 Earthshot Prize awards event. This visit marks their first overseas engagement together since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The awards will bring together notable personalities and focus on environmental challenges and innovation. Kate has been gradually returning to public life after her recovery, which has had its challenges.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Jimothy Card Auction: Rare card sells for $20,100; proceeds may fund Abby’s college
item.description: A young baseball enthusiast from Seattle secured an esteemed baseball card during a Mariners game. This unique card showcased Jimothy, a raccoon who captured the internet's attention due to his extraordinary look. Initially a complimentary giveaway, the card has now emerged as a remarkable collectible valued at an astonishing $20,100. With multiple offers pouring in, her family decided to auction it on eBay, generating significant buzz.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A bronze leg found in 1820 considered Roman loot now believed to belong to a statue of Antoninus Pius
item.description: Emperor Antoninus Pius, celebrated for his peace-driven rule and military expeditions, may have a newly discovered connection to history. A bronze leg unearthed in Scotland suggests a statue that honored him was disassembled by Roman forces prior to their withdrawal in AD 161, challenging prior beliefs of theft. This discovery sheds light on how Rome strategically managed its monuments, and further archaeological investigations could reveal more insights.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
